statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n integers. Turn the array into a min-heap in place using the bottom-up build: for i from the last internal node (n/2 - 1) down to 0, sift index i down - swap it with its smaller child while some child is smaller. Print the resulting array, space-separated. This exact procedure is deterministic, so your output must match it precisely; it runs in linear total time because deep nodes sift only short distances.

example.why: Only index 1 moves: 20 swaps with its smaller child 12; indices 2 and 0 already satisfy the promise.

hint: Sift down swaps with the smaller child - the smaller child is the only value safe to place above the other.
mistake: Running i upward from 0; sift-down assumes the subtrees below are already heaps, so build backwards.
